title: Transient page leak under continuous batching — tracing harness & mitigations
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Summary: Intermittent GPU resident page growth observed under sustained continuous-batching load with KV cache warming. RSS increases over long tails (3–12 hours) despite apparent successful evictions; growth correlates with periods of rapid small allocations and stream-synchronization events. This ticket implements a tracing harness to capture allocator return-paths, stream fence timing, and per-stream outstanding cudaMallocAsync allocations to root-cause transient 'orphaned' pages that are not reclaimed by the multipool.

Observed behavior: On a canary workload (batching enabled, variable sequence length, KV warmup enabled) we see a slow-but-steady growth in device RSS from 62GB to 85GB over 8 hours on a 96GB GPU. Process-level metrics show no increase in logical allocations; the allocator's pool accounting reports deallocated blocks but resident pages remain. gpu_top/resident reports show pages pinned to stream IDs that become inactive. Repro is non-deterministic but higher probability when background prefetch jobs and concurrent small user batches interleave.

Hypotheses:
- cudaMallocAsync deferred free path is being delayed by stream-quiescence waits: freed extents remain resident until last stream event completes, but fences can be missed when using user CUs and the runtime defers completion.
- KV cache warmup prefetches allocate pinned staging arenas on ephemeral streams; when those streams are destroyed rapidly, the allocator fails to return pages to the OS due to slab fragmentation and sub-chunk bookkeeping inconsistencies.
- A race between multipool coalescer and async free triggers a state where a slab is marked free in metadata but never added back to the free list (shadow state) causing resident pages to persist.

Scope: Build a low-overhead tracing harness that records per-allocation metadata (alloc size, pool id, stream id, event timestamps) and correlates with kernel and stream activity. Add deterministic microbench reproducer that flips between heavy prefetch and small user batch workloads to increase repro rate.

Reproduction steps (dev cluster):
1) Deploy canary runtime build runtime-1.19-canary on a single 96GB A100 node in staging.
2) Run repro harness: tests/mem_repro/prefetch_vs_smallbatch.py --batches=10000 --kv-warmup=on --prefetch-concurrency=6
3) Capture allocator traces: /tmp/alloc-trace-$(timestamp).log (enabled via ENV RN_ALLOC_TRACE=1)
4) Monitor: nvidia-smi, /proc/<pid>/smaps, and internal metric allocator.resident_pages by pool.

Telemetry to capture: per-allocation id, callsite (symbolized), cudaStream_t hex id, cudaEvent timestamps (alloc/free), slab id, pool bucket, host pinned vs device pages, and backlog of pending frees.

Experiments run so far:
- Experiment A (2025-01-14): Added quick-event insertion on free path; repro rate decreased from ~1/50 runs to ~1/300 but not eliminated. Logs indicate pending event backlog still present when repro occurs.
- Experiment B (2025-01-16): Force synchronous cudaDeviceSynchronize after prefetch teardown; immediate reclamation occurred but increased latency and caused minor throughput regression. Indicates stream quiescence related.
- Experiment C (2025-01-18): Adjusted multipool coalescer to prefer immediate coalesce for slabs with >80% free; reduced resident growth but did not remove rare long-tail cases.

Proposed plan (tasks):
- Task 1: Implement tracing harness in allocator: record per-allocation stream_id, event_id, free_reason, and stack-trace sampling (low overhead). Attach to RN_ALLOC_TRACE env flag. (owner: Marco)
- Task 2: Microbench suite: deterministic interleaving between prefetch streams and user streams to increase repro probability. Add option to pin CPU threads to reduce scheduling noise. (owner: Priya Rao)
- Task 3: Correlate trace outputs with kernel traces (nsys) for sampled reproductions; generate timeline visualizer (simple flame chart) for stream events vs allocator actions. (owner: Marco)
- Task 4: Implement mitigation toggle: conservative eager-return path that forces cudaFreeAsync fallback for slabs older than threshold T in staging; measure latency and throughput impact. (owner: Aisha)
- Task 5: If root cause is bookkeeping race, prepare atomic-state patch and add unit tests for slab lifecycle transitions under concurrent stream destruction. (owner: Marco)

Acceptance criteria:
- Tracing harness reproducibly captures orphaned allocation lifecycles and exposes at least one deterministic root-cause sequence in 90% of repro runs on the microbench.
- Mitigation toggle reduces resident growth to <5% over 12 hours under the reproduced workload with <10% p99 latency regression.
- Patch to allocator with tests merged and rollout plan for runtime-1.19.

Notes and links:
- Initial logs and sample traces: https://drive.redwood.ai/memory/ENG-934210/traces
- Microbench: github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/tree/main/tests/mem_repro
- Design doc (root-cause theories and instrumentation): https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/RUNTIME/ENG-934210
comments: 2025-01-13 — Marco Chen: Started initial trace shim in alloc layer. Instrumentation added to record stream pointer and cudaEvent pair for each async alloc/free. Running overnight batch to collect samples.
2025-01-14 — Priya Rao (QA): Microbench improved; increased prefetch concurrency to 6 and lowered inter-request jitter. Repro rate jumped to ~1/50. Uploading sample logs to Drive link in description.
2025-01-16 — Aisha Patel (PM): Reviewed experiment results. Eager-sync mitigation shows reclamation but unacceptable latency hit for PLG workloads. Keep as fallback toggle only.

2025-01-18 — Marco Chen: Correlated allocator traces with nsys snapshots; found one sequence where free event posted on stream A but final event occurred on stream B after stream destruction, causing allocator to mark slab freed but never reclaim page due to missing reinsert into free list. Draft patch attempted to check event ownership; needs deeper atomicity fix.
